item.title: The Zenwalker (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
A tragic complex story of a powerful entity playing hero only to become the only threat he ever had to worry about.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Cosmic Horror, Drama/Emotional,

Page Layout (Optional): This is going to be a rare case of and scp article in an scp article. There will be the normal containment procedures followed by a description then an addendum containing an scp article about this scp that he brought with him from the future (I know, bare with me). After the addendum, logs reviewing the interviews with the scp.

Elevator Pitch: Basically, this scp is an anomalous man from a different dimension in which the laws of physics are fundamentally different. It's because of this difference that he has the ability to manipulate gravity. His upbringing and childlike curiosity provided the perfect origin story for a modern superhero with a scientific alter ego. By day he was a lab coat pushing the limits of his abilities to fully understand gravity and it's effects, by night a merciless vigilante obliterating local crime with an iron fist.

+ show block
– hide block

Now, I know what it looks like but stay with me, this isn't just another superhero. In fact, the true danger of this scp came from his day job as a scientist. His continuous experiments yielded amazing discoveries about what he could do, but it eventually led to the collapse of the universe as we know it. The collapse of the universe damned him to just exist in an existence in which he was the only thing that excited. Madness had claimed him after a millennia of solitude, but he didn't spend his time in the void laying down. He used this time to further study his ability. Eventually he was able to feel the connection between time and gravity. This led his ability to manipulate time. From there he formulated a plan to send himself back in time to kill his younger self before he collapses the universe. However, do to his mental instability he was slain his younger self. That younger version of himself grew to repeat history/the future and collapsed the universe, went mad, discovered time travel, and repeated the plan to kill his younger self. This time however, he remembered how he defeated his older self and didn't fall for the same tactic he used when he was younger. This caused the fight to last a while longer than the first fight. However, the younger version of himself still came out on top do to his mental edge. This younger version of himself repeated the same cycle extending the fight just a bit longer. As the cycle continued the scale of the battle grew larger, so did the foundation's involvement. This only served to escalate the situation as it eventually led to a broken masquerade. This cycle repeated until the battle was the cause of the collapsed universe. The cycle finally ended when he decided to instead travel farther back in time and seek out the foundation to contain his younger self before he grows up to become a threat. The conversation with a mad man didn't get nearly as far as the scp article he brought back with him as proof of his claims. The article inside the article is the one he brought back with him and the over all article will be the whole story.

Central Narrative: It's a tragic story of a hero being his only threat. Eventually ending the narrative before it starts.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The very deeply rooted story.

Additional Notes: This is my first attribution to the site in general and I'm sure I have a lot to learn. This is me diving head first into a community I've loved for years and should have contributed to ages ago. All criticism welcome and appreciated.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. Also, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 130 words over. Please address this before seeking further feedback. ~Zyn
Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: The Zenwalker (Seeking Greenlight)

Shouldn't the several hundred additional entities receive SCP designations? Shouldn't the Foundation perhaps take an interest in establishing communication with this species, if only in order to negotiate a less Veil-endangering place for them to portal in next time?

The Foundation presented in this scip seems amateurish and sloppy. Even compliant sentient entities are nontrivial to contain. It doesn't help that we're just offhandedly told that the second round of containment was successful, easy peasy, as if the evaluator is carefree and disinterested. There isn't even a cliché note about administering amnestics to witnesses.

I guess I'm in the minority, given that the article has 150+ upvotes. It's not all bad. I like the anomaly itself. I think its use of Yelp is cute, in a good way. But even the more cringe-inducing articles of the LOLFoundation era don't present this cavalier an institution.

item.title: Human Fungi
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX represents a single species of fungi, currently only known to exist within northern Queensland, Australia. SCP-XXXX is similar to the genus Ophiocordyceps, as SCP-XXXX has the ability to infect Insectoids, Birds, and Mamalians including Humans. Once an individual has been infected with SCP-XXXX (now designated SCP-XXXX-1) during early stages will begin to suppress the individual's consciousness and hijack the brain. SCP-XXXX has the ability to tap into the memories of SCP-XXXX-1, because of this SCP-XXXX-1 are able to basic human things such as communicating, movement, etc

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX during late stages will use the SCP-XXXX-1 instance to move to a suitable location to multiply. Once achieved SCP-XXXX-1 will attach itself to a surface, as well as immobilising itself by placing a cocoon like structure around its body. From here spores will begin to fly out of SCP-XXXX-1, which will multiply SCP-XXXX

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Numerous SCP-XXXX-1 instances have been leaked (and deleted of course) however one was able to communicate directly to an non-infected individual via text. This is where the story will take place.

item.title: Re: Edit SCP or new tale?
item.content:encoded:
I don't want to bea nudge about this, but I also had an idea to make this a joke SCP and I just want to run the idea to see if it's actually funny or if it's just me.

There are multiple instances of SCP-2806, and multiple instances can be designated by number or letter. In this case they are numbered, but that's for the instances when they are not connected to a human, so what if the humans still connected were designated by letter?

So my guy comes in, clearly a Mary Sue, the data entry worker checks the file and sees that about 200 of these guys could be coming through and decides to designate this instance 2806-J just so he can be purposely misfiled as a joke SCP even though he's not a joke. So the real joke is that he's actually totally legit but nobody takes him seriously because of a prank in records and his career is ruined.

I honestly don't know whether that's funny enough to work, so feel free to shoot it down.

item.title: Re: Finding the Scarlet King's children.
item.content:encoded:
In the Serpent's Hand Hub, SCP-017 is called the Second Child which I assume is the second child of the Scarlet King. Also Summer's Exile which is about SCP-682 mentions the Fifth Child which suggests SCP-053, and my theory is the reason that those two get along is because they are siblings, or at least half-siblings, with SCP-682 being first generation and SCP-053 being second generation from the same father, the Scarlet King.

And then of course, there's the story about SCP-999 being the seventh child, which now accounts for three of the six surviving children, assuming the fourth is still dead. My guess is SCP-239 and SCP-040 are two others, and while I doubt it could work by context, I think it would be intesting to reveal SCP-105 is actually the first child of the Scarlet King and that Team Iris of Alpha-9 is critical in defeating him the next time he breaks free.

One of my absolute favorite SCPs. There's just enough there to piece together the narrative, and it's a good narrative. And it easily has one of the best first person descents into madness I've seen in any horror story, and I've seen a lot of those.

Some possibly spoilery thoughts:

+ show block
– hide block

I interpret the light as destroying the metaphysical "anchor" that keeps something squarely in a single reality, making it exist in multiple parallel realities at once, maybe even every possible reality at once. That's why the researcher says they're not ready for "what's out there"; every possible reality in the Foundation's carefully monitored test chambers is much easier to deal with than the chaos of the world outside. This idea fits in with Star Signals, which describes the Fifth World as your ideal version of reality, the universe sculpted by you into your perfect shape. By severing your connection to one single world, the light gives you the freedom to move to any world. But the human mind isn't made for this, and very strange things happen to a person when they do this.

Most assume the 'body' referred to in "Don't worry about the body" must be a corpse, but I think that line should actually be taken as a much more general statement. As in, don't worry about the physical body, the mind is what matters. Given 3005's general effects on human bodies, this seems like solid advice.

Honestly, I love this SCP, along with 1425, so much that I have trouble accepting any other take on the Fifth Church into my personal headcanon, which I suppose is ironic given the subject material.

Forum thread: SCP-3005

I am really teetering on the edge of an upvote for this one. To be clear, I really like the story itself, but…

The one problem I have with this is that I just can't see the Foundation letting any of this happen. I can buy the doctors being sassy as all hell, because, they kinda work in an actual hellscape and humour is a major coping mechanism. The problem I do have is that the Foundation isn't incompetent and is very strict about following the rules (at least in my headcannon). That whole section charter quote, in my headcannon, is not a slap on the wrist kind of violation (did she even get that much?). For me, that would be grounds for immediate and pretty severe disciplinary action.

As I said, I like the story, so it's not even close to a downvote, but this just really messes with how I view the Foundation (and not in a good way). Ah well, I hope this opinion isn't completely outlandish to you. I look forward to seeing more (and hopefully upvoting next time)

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the feedback. I will try and clarify a few things:

+ Clarifications
- Close

Why is this happening?

Because over the years many people have became intangible and fallen to the center of the earth.

Why is the majority of objects at the center “human corpses”?

Because humans are the most common thing to turn intangible and fall through the fall due to our natural desire for power, in this case, the power to walk through walls. Naturally there are also other animals and inanimate objects in there as well.

How is it possible that they number in the billions?

This anomaly has been building up over many thousands of years. The bodies come from as far-flung sources as ancient trickster gods, experimental para-technology from an Occult war and quite a few from previous iterations of SCP-2000. Lastly while most bodies are dead, none have decomposed due to their intangible nature.

Why are the agents “blind, deaf and mute”? If so, how do they even use a computer?

The agents are "blind, deaf and mute" due to how their eyes ears and mouths are located entirely within the solid matter of the earth inner core. They use a computer because it was in contact with one of them when they became intangible, staying intangible as well and allowing the intangible agent to use it.

Similarly, why does the effect suddenly wear off and they die?

Because all types of intangibly eventually wear off after a certain amount of time within a solid or liquid. They agents die when they become tangible enough to suffocate.

Lastly, the Foundation not pursuing containment of the anomaly is not in line with their motto.

The Foundation isn't containing it because:
1. It's effectively self-containing due to it's location.
2. There is not feasible way to remove it from it's location.
3. The threat to exposure to the public is extremely small.
4. If they were somehow able to remove it, it would inevitably end up there again upon the first containment breach.

Basically, the MTF goes incorporeal, communicate with the Foundation, and then they die? You need more than that, especially if you want to give your readers some semblance of answers as to what’s going on.

The narrative of the article is the story of that MTF and their gradual transformation from hopeful, to weary to despairing and begging for rescue. At first they help the foundation in any way they can by communicating with them an informing them of the anomaly and trying to help them document it. After a while they realize they won't be rescued. As for answers, there are none. This isn't a sinister plot or experiment gone wrong, this is an inevitability in a world with intangibility.

> Other suggestions might be to explain the origins of the anomaly, how/why the CI is involved and how exactly the Foundation goes about trying to contain this.

1. The anomaly is the collection of everyone who has ever become intangible and fallen through the floor.
2. The CI is a plot device explaining how an entire MTF was turned intangible. They have little importance to the anomaly overall. The CI could be change to the SH or an experiment gone wrong.
3. The Foundation can't/won't/doesn't need to contain the anomaly due to it's nature, being content with observation and documentation.

Hope this clear a few things up!


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth

I have two big problems with this. The first is a matter of personal taste; I just don't find the anomaly interesting. Despite O5-11's insistence to the contrary, I don't see this as meaningfully distinct from the concept of Hell, and I've simply heard about plenty of versions of Hell already. It's not an interesting or creative idea of Hell either. Everything hurts really badly forever, the end. Sure, it's horrifying, but not in a compelling way, which is a letdown considering how much buildup it gets.

The second issue I have with this article is something I'm surprised no one seems to have brought up yet, though I didn't go through all the comments, so maybe someone did. I cannot remotely believe that the Overseers would ever allow one of their own to leave for vacation without notice and with no way to contact them. I can handle an Overseer speaking in purple prose, some people really do that. I can accept the idea of the Overseers using anomalies on themselves, it's maybe not the wisest choice, but it's a choice I can picture some version of the Council making. But letting each other vanish without notice? That wouldn't fly at a regular job, much less for leaders of a worldwide top secret agency tasked with the fate of humanity. I know they said they banned the practice after 11 went missing, but I simply can't suspend my disbelief nearly enough to picture them ever allowing it in the first place. How are they supposed to tell if Roger is on one of his weekend trips, or if he's been captured by the Insurgency or something? The logical dissonance was too much for me to stay invested in the article. I did love 11 jumping in with 106 though, that was a great 'oh shit' moment.

This has been my favorite SCP for years. It’s so deeply unsettling and equally intriguing.

My interpretation:

+ show block
– hide block

I think Olivia might not literally be their daughter. I think she might be the knot in reality that clearly exists inescapably intertwined with this family manifesting itself as a person. Specifically, I think she might be the personification of her 'parent's' screwed up relationship that they can no longer address. It seems that, according to them, they have her, and then three other much younger kids who are close in age. That's an odd pattern in which to have children. I'm thinking it's because 'Olivia' has existed since the start of their relationship, because she is a part of their relationship, and she takes the form of their child because she's something they created together. That's why they can't move, can't leave, can't get away from the house. Because the anomaly isn't really in the attic. It's in them.

Or, well, that's a clear, logical explanation. But I don't think this SCP really has a clear, logical explanation behind it. I used to have these fucked up dreams where my family's late rabbit is alive again and we haven't been taking care of her for so long and I feel like we failed her and I don't know when or how she's going to leave again, and because of that I feel like I know EXACTLY what this SCP is, but not in a way that means I can explain it.
